content: The International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease, based in Paris, France, is a key organization in the fight against tuberculosis (TB) and lung diseases. Mike Frick, from the TB/HIV Project at the Treatment Action Group in New York, USA, is actively involved in addressing the intersection of TB and HIV. Andrei Mariandyshev, the Head of the Phthisiopulmonary Department in Arkhangelsk, Russian Federation, contributes his expertise in clinical and public health aspects of TB. Nguyen Viet Nhung, the Director of the National Lung Hospital and Manager of the National TB Programme in Hanoi, Vietnam, oversees TB care and prevention strategies in the region. Ejaz Qadeer, from the Ministry of Health in Islamabad, Pakistan, plays a significant role in national TB control efforts. Abdul Hamid Salim, an advisor to the National TB Programme in Bangladesh, focuses on global funding and multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) initiatives. The World Health Organization (WHO) has consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis care and support, including contributions from Simon Schaaf, a pediatrician specializing in pediatric MDR-TB and surveillance at Stellenbosch University in South Africa. Holger Schünemann, a methodologist at McMaster University in Canada, chaired the guideline development group. Pedro Guillermo Suarez, from Management Sciences for Health in Arlington, USA, provided input but was unable to attend the meeting. Carrie Tudor, the TB Project Director at the International Council of Nurses in Durban, South Africa, and Justin Wong Yun Yaw, Head of the Disease Control Division at the Ministry of Health in Brunei, also contributed to the discussions. Evidence reviewers included Narges Alipanah from Santa Clara Valley Medical Center in the USA, Lelia Chaisson from Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, Jennifer Ho from the Woolcock Institute of Medical Research at the University of Sydney, and James Johnston from the British Columbia Centre for Disease Control in Canada. Dick Menzies from the Montreal Chest Institute and Payam Nahid, a professor at the University of California, San Francisco, also reviewed evidence for the guidelines. Observers at the guideline development meetings included Amy Bloom from the US Agency for International Development (USAID) in Washington, DC, and Janet Ginnard from UNITAID in Geneva, Switzerland. The WHO headquarters secretariat, led by the Global TB Programme, included experts such as Annabel Baddley, Dennis Falzon, Giuliano Gargioni, and others who provided technical and administrative support. The external review group included Mohammed Aziz from the WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean, Masoud Dara from the WHO Regional Office for Europe, and Riitta Dlodlo from the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in France. Other contributors included Celine Garfin from the Ministry of Health in the Philippines, Mirtha del Granado from the WHO Regional Office for the Americas, and Daniel Kibuga from the WHO Regional Office for Africa. Experts involved in the development of the guidelines included Vaira Leimane from the Riga East University Hospital in Latvia, Nobuyuki Nishikiori from the WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, and Lee Reichman from Rutgers New Jersey Medical School in the USA. Rohit Sarin from the National Institute of TB and Respiratory Diseases in India and Dalene von Delft from TB Proof in South Africa also provided critical input. Technical resource persons and observers included Pete Dodd from Sheffield University in the UK, Anneke Hesseling from Stellenbosch University in South Africa, and Oliver Marcy from the University of Bordeaux in France. Nicole Salazar-Austin from Johns Hopkins University and James Seddon from Imperial College London served as technical resource persons during the guideline development group meetings. The WHO Steering Group for the guidelines included members from various WHO departments and regional offices, such as Annabel Baddley, Ernesto Jaramillo, and Martina Penazzato. They worked collaboratively to ensure the guidelines addressed the needs of TB patients globally. The guideline development group (GDG) for drug-resistant TB treatment included Jaime Bayona from Socios En Salud in Peru, José A. Caminero from the University General Hospital of Gran Canaria in Spain, and Charles L. Daley from National Jewish Health in the USA. Other members included Agnes Gebhard from the Royal Dutch Tuberculosis Foundation in the Netherlands, Myriam Henckens from Médecins Sans Frontières in France, and Timothy H. Holtz from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Thailand. The evidence review teams included experts such as Chunling Lu and Carole D. Mitnick from Harvard Medical School, Richard A. White from the Harvard School of Public Health, and Gail Kennedy from the University of California, San Francisco. They conducted systematic reviews to inform the guideline recommendations. The guidelines address critical questions related to TB care and support interventions, including adherence to treatment, outcomes of conventional TB treatment, adverse reactions to TB drugs, and the cost implications for patients and health services. Specific models of care for MDR-TB and TB prevention in high-burden settings were also evaluated, with a focus on decentralized treatment and ambulatory therapy. The guidelines emphasize the importance of tailored care models for children and adolescents, as well as the integration of TB care with other health conditions such as HIV, diabetes, and chronic lung diseases. The recommendations aim to improve treatment adherence, reduce drug resistance, and enhance patient outcomes while minimizing costs to both patients and health systems. This version maintains the detailed information while presenting it in a clear and professional manner suitable for medical experts.
